To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a graph-theoretically characterization of structural controllable multi-agent systems under switching topology.

a graph-theoretically characterized condition for structural controllability can be derived for multi-agent systems with switching topologies, and that this condition is based on the connectivity of the union graph G.

the multi-agent systems with switching topologies can be structurally controllable even though they may not be controllable under each individual communication topology, and that the multi-agent with switching topology is controllable if and if only the union graph of the communication topologies is a connected graph.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a graph-theoretically characterization of the structural properties of a networked multi-agent system.
a graph-theoretically characterization of the structural stability of multi-agent systems, which is a generalization to the traditional stability analysis for dynamical systems.
the structural controllabil- ity problem for multi-agent system under switching topology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structural controllablity of multi-agent systems under switching topologies can be determined by the union graph of the underlying communication topologies.
the structural controllablity of the multi-agent system under consideration is a function of the union graph of the underlay communication topology.
a multi-agent system with a single leader is structurally controllability if and only if G is connected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the graph-theoretic approach is a powerful tool for studying structural controllability and its application to multi-agent system.
we have provided the necessary and sufficient conditions for multi-agent systems with switching topology to be structurally controllable.
we have provided a necessary and sufficient condition for the structural controllablity of a multi-agent system with a single leader and switching topology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural controllabiliy is determined by the underlying graph of communication topology, regardless of switching topology.
structural controllability is a graph-theoretical concept.
the structural controllabilty of a multi-agent system with a single leader is purely determined by the communication topologies, and it is independent of the switching sequence.
